text:
Marcus Lin: Doing a pass on Dedicated staged rollouts audit logging before we lock beta. Need to confirm: event types, required fields, retention, and mapping to SOC2 controls. Can folks sanity check what we’re planning?

Ethan Park: sure. we’ve got PR up for event emission (create/update/approve/abort + evaluator auto-hold). what’s missing?

Kevin Osei: also want to make sure these events flow through the existing audit export pipeline (S3 + SIEM). We’ve been burned by “new audit logs” that are only in app logs.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 and RBAC: which roles can view the audit entries? Dedicated tenants will ask.

Marcus Lin: Current list from PRD/ADR draft:
- rollout.plan.create
- rollout.plan.update
- rollout.stage.approve
- rollout.stage.abort
- rollout.stage.auto_hold (gate failed OR missing metrics)
- rollout.stage.auto_rollback (if we support v1?)
- rollout.plan.delete (are we allowing delete?)
We need to decide what’s required for SOC2 evidence and what’s nice-to-have.

Chloe Martin: delete is not in v1. we were going to do “disable” / create a new version. So no plan.delete event.

Ethan Park: agreed. objects are versioned; “update” creates new plan_version. We can record update events + diff summary.

Sean Gallagher: from SRE side: auto_hold needs to be explicit and include reason + gate snapshot. during incident review we need to answer “why did it pause / why did it proceed”.

Allison Grant: + include evaluator health. If auto_hold is triggered due to missing metrics / evaluator degraded, we should distinguish those (metrics_late vs threshold_breach vs evaluator_lag).

Marcus Lin: ok. Let’s talk fields. For SOC2 we typically need: who did what, when, on what system, and whether it succeeded. For rollouts we also need tenant/pool scoping.
Proposed required fields (min):
- event_type
- event_ts
- actor_type (user/service)
- actor_id (user_id or service name)
- actor_ip (if user-originated)
- tenant_id
- pool_id (dedicated pool)
- rollout_plan_id
- plan_version
- stage_id (if stage action)
- request_id / trace_id
- outcome (success/failure)
- reason (freeform + enumerated code)
Does this cover everyone’s needs?

Kevin Osei: please add: 
- authn_context (sso, api_key, internal_operator)
- authz_decision_id (tie to policy engine decision log)
- idempotency_key (for approve/abort endpoints) 
This helps correlate duplicates + detective controls.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: also “acting_as” for internal ops doing actions on behalf of tenant. we need to represent impersonation / breakglass.

Chloe Martin: our auth layer already passes `actor_subject` + optional `delegated_tenant`. can include that. We can add `impersonation=true` and `impersonated_user_id` when applicable.

Ethan Park: re: stage_id — stage is stable within a plan_version. we generate stage UUIDs. for human readability we can also include stage_name and stage_weight.

Sean Gallagher: gate snapshot: for auto_hold we should store the evaluated metric + threshold at decision time. Doesn’t have to be full timeseries, but enough to see “p95 latency 1.9s > 1.2s threshold over last 10m”.

Allison Grant: careful on payload bloat / PII. Latency/error/util is fine. Don’t include prompts or request bodies. We should explicitly state that audit events must not contain customer data.

Marcus Lin: yep. We'll enforce a schema with allowed keys + size limits. No prompts/inputs. For “diff” on plan.update, keep it to config keys (e.g., gate thresholds changed) and redacted where needed.

Kevin Osei: retention: what are we committing to? SOC2 evidence usually expects >= 1 year of audit logs. Some customers ask for 400 days / 13 months. A few regulated ones ask for 7 years but that’s usually a separate export contract.

Marcus Lin: My proposal:
- Default retention in Redwood audit store: 400 days (gives buffer beyond 365)
- Export pipeline: customer-configurable via existing audit export (they can keep longer in their SIEM)
- For internal operator events: same 400 days in audit store; backups follow standard retention.
Thoughts?

Sean Gallagher: 400 days works. Operationally we usually look back 30–90 days but postmortems sometimes need longer.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: what about Dedicated enterprise tenants viewing logs in Console? if we only keep 30 days in UI but 400 in backend, customers will complain.

Chloe Martin: we can paginate audit events in Console. I’d rather align UI retention with backend (400) but maybe default UI filters to 30 days.

Kevin Osei: fine as long as backend is 400 and we have an SLA on export delivery. Also: immutability / tamper-evidence. SOC2 CC6/CC7 doesn’t require WORM strictly but we should have integrity controls.

Marcus Lin: Mapping to SOC2-style controls (draft):
- CC6.1 / CC6.2 (logical access): record privileged actions (approve/abort/edit) with actor + auth context
- CC7.2 (change management): record rollout plan updates and approvals; provide audit trail for changes to production configs
- CC7.3 (monitoring): auto_hold events based on gates show automated detection + response
- CC7.4 (incident response): link rollout actions to incident timelines via request_id/trace_id; supports investigations
- CC8.1 (system operations): retention + restricted access to audit logs
Does this mapping make sense?

Kevin Osei: yes. also add: “audit log access is itself audited” (meta-auditing). we already emit `auditlog.read` events for export + console views, right?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: we do for export jobs; console reads might not be instrumented consistently. if we can’t do `auditlog.read` by beta, at least ensure access is restricted (RBAC) and document gap.

Marcus Lin: I’d like to avoid promising read-auditing unless it’s real. Can we add console read events quickly?

Chloe Martin: might be non-trivial to avoid noise, but we can emit read events only for “download/export” actions in Console, not every page view. That’s probably enough for evidence.

Ethan Park: on the service side we can tag the audit retrieval endpoint with `purpose=interactive_view` vs `purpose=export_download` and only emit for the latter.

Allison Grant: +1, otherwise we drown in read logs. For SOC2, “download” is the risky action.

Marcus Lin: Great. Next: where stored and how protected.
Requirements I’m putting in security notes:
- Write-only path from services -> audit pipeline (no updates/deletes)
- Stored encrypted at rest (KMS), access limited to Security/Compliance + oncall breakglass
- Export to SIEM uses least privilege role, logs access by export job
- Schema validation + max size (prevent injection / PII leaks)
Anything else?

Kevin Osei: include: clock source. Use server-side timestamp in collector to avoid clients spoofing event_ts. Still store service-provided ts as “observed_ts” if you want.

Ethan Park: we can do both: `event_ts` (service) + `ingested_ts` (collector). The collector is the source of truth for ordering.

Sean Gallagher: also: if evaluator is degraded and forces hold, that action should be an audit event with actor_type=service and a reason code like `evaluator_degraded_fail_safe`.

Marcus Lin: yes, that’s explicitly SOC2-friendly: automated control that fails safe.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC scope question: who can view audit events?
- Internal: operator + security
- Tenant: org admins + dedicated ops role
Need to ensure tenant can’t see other tenants’ pool_ids.

Chloe Martin: audit query requires tenant_id and is filtered server-side. For internal, we’ll require `auditlog.view_all` permission. For tenant scope: `auditlog.view`.

Marcus Lin: please document this in ADR-028 / security doc.

Connor O'Brien: jumping in re retention: any risk with 400 days + volume? dedicated rollouts could be chatty if gates evaluate frequently.

Allison Grant: evaluator tick shouldn’t emit audit events every tick. Only emit when state changes (hold, advance, rollback) + manual actions. Metrics are separate.

Ethan Park: yup. We emit audit events on state transitions only. Gate evaluation details attached to the transition event.

Kevin Osei: ok. One more: event naming + stability. Customers will build parsers. we should version the schema or guarantee backward compat.

Marcus Lin: Add `schema_version=1` field, and we’ll only add optional fields. Breaking changes require new version + deprecation window.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: can we ensure `actor_id` is stable (UUID) vs email? avoid PII.

Chloe Martin: yes, user_id. For human readability in Console we resolve to display name via separate lookup (not in the audit event payload).

Marcus Lin: action items:
1) Chloe/Ethan: confirm event types list (no delete), add reason codes + schema_version
2) Kevin: confirm export pipeline handles new event types + include authn_context + ingested_ts
3) Kaitlyn: finalize RBAC matrix for view vs export/download + impersonation fields
4) Allison/Sean: define minimal gate snapshot fields + ensure no PII
I’ll update the security doc + SOC2 control mapping accordingly.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. :thumbsup:

Kevin Osei: :thumbsup: pls loop me on the sample event examples; I’ll run through SIEM parsing.

Chloe Martin: will do. I’ll post examples once the PR lands in staging.

Marcus Lin: thanks all. keeping this thread open for any customer-specific retention asks; default stays 400d + export for longer.
